This is actually one of Uplands cleaner data points. Operating cash flow (CFO) for FY2025 was  $25.8M , which compares favorably to the accounting net loss of  -$44.75M — the gap is explained mostly by non-cash charges like depreciation and amortization ( $32.14M for the year) and stock-based compensation ( $9.11M ). In the two most recent quarters, CFO was  $7.32M in Q4 2025 and  $5.60M in Q1 2026. FCF (after minimal capex of  $0.09M and  $0.08M respectively) was  $7.23M and  $5.52M . These are real cash flows. One thing to watch: in Q4 2025, receivables increased by  $6.6M (a use of cash), which partially dragged on CFO, but the quarter still produced positive operating cash flow. In Q1 2026, receivables fell by  $1.87M (a source of cash), helping CFO. Deferred revenue — a key metric for software companies because it represents cash collected before service is delivered — was  $74.77M at year-end and  $73.75M in Q1 2026, a slight decline of about  $1M . In Q4 2025, deferred revenue increased by  $7.78M , which boosted cash flow. The FCF margin of  11.34% in Q1 2026 and  14.66% in Q4 2025 are above the FY2025 annual level of  11.27% , showing quarterly cash conversion is actually holding up reasonably well relative to the shrinking revenue base.

  Despite the losses and balance sheet deterioration, Upland produced positive free cash flow (FCF — operating cash after spending on equipment and infrastructure) in every single year of the five-year window. FCF was  $41M in FY2021, dipped to  $29M in FY2022, surged to  $49M in FY2023, fell back to  $23M in FY2024, and recovered slightly to  $24M in FY2025. The five-year average FCF is roughly  $33M per year. Capex (capital expenditures — money spent on physical assets) remained tiny, ranging between  $0.87M and  $1.35M annually — typical for an asset-light software business.

### Ziff Davis (ZD) Q1 CY2026 Highlights:

*   **Revenue:** $267.6 million vs analyst estimates of $287.4 million (18.6% year-on-year decline, 6.9% miss)
*   **Adjusted EPS:** $0.73 vs analyst expectations of $0.77 (5.1% miss)

“We remain focused on unlocking value for our shareholders as we look to complete the divestiture of the Connectivity business as well as explore additional value-creating transactions,” said Vivek Shah, CEO of Ziff Davis.

### Company Overview

## Summary

Ziff Davis reported Q1 revenue of $267.6 million, a 1.9% decline Y/Y. The operating landscape remains challenged, as operating income fell 80% to $2.9 million. Margin compression was pronounced, with operating margins narrowing by 4.2 percentage points to 1.1%, down from 5.3% in the prior-year period. Adjusted EBITDA decreased 11.2% Y/Y to $63.4 million.

Segment performance varied. Tech & Shopping, a core segment, saw revenue contract 12.9% to $71.1 million, acting as a drag on consolidated results. Conversely, Cybersecurity & Martech grew 3.6% to $69.8 million, and Gaming & Entertainment rose 7.2% to $40.8 million, providing partial offsets to the weakness in Tech & Shopping.

The company suspended its full-year 2026 guidance, citing the ongoing divestiture of the Connectivity business. This unit is now classified as held for sale, creating uncertainty regarding the company's consolidated earnings baseline and future resource allocation.

Capital allocation remains a central focus. Free cash flow was negative $(3.2) million, yet management deployed $51.6 million toward share repurchases during the quarter. This divergence between cash flow generation and stock buybacks highlights the strategy to return capital despite current operational headwinds. The success of the Connectivity divestiture, including the deployment of proceeds, will be critical to the future financial profile.
